tone_statements.citation: Gawne, Lauren. 2019. A grammatical overview of Yolmo (Tibeto-Burman). WikiJournal of Humanities 2(1):2, 1-23. doi:10.15347/wjh/2019.002
tone_statements.quote: In Yohlmo the domain for contrastive tones is the morpheme, and it is the first syllable of the morpheme which is most significant for the realization of tone contours. The primary supra-segmental contrast is the Register Contrast: high and low register. ... The secondary supra-segmental contrast is realized by different Pitch Contours: In the high register, we find that a basically level contour contrasts with a high, falling contour; and in the low register a basically level contour contrasts with a mid, falling contour.
tone_statements.locator: p.14, sec. 2.4 'Tonal contrasts'; tone numbers/labels from Table 2 'Tonal contrasts and their phonological representation' and Table 3, p.15
tone_statements.summary: Four contrastive tones per morpheme: high vs low (breathy) register, each with a basically level and a falling contour; register contrast robust, contours subtle; mainly on the first syllable.

tone_statements.citation: Gawne, Lauren. 2013. Report on the relationship between Yolmo and Kagate. Himalayan Linguistics 12(2): 1-27. doi:10.5070/h912223716
tone_statements.quote: The domain for the contrastive tones is the morphemes. It is the first syllable which is most significant for the realization of tone contours. The basic suprasegmental contrast is the register contrast: high and low registers. Secondary suprasegmental contrast is realized by different pitch contours. Yolhmo is close to central Tibetan in tonogenesis. Register and tone contrast came from the same source. Historically, the register contrast is derived from the original voicing status and cluster compositions of the morpheme initial consonant margins.

tone_statements.summary: Summarising Hari: tone contrasts per morpheme, first syllable decisive; basic contrast is register, high vs low, plus a secondary contrast of pitch contours (uncounted, unnamed); down-drift noted.

tone_statements.citation: Hari, Anna Maria (2010). Yohlmo grammar sketch. Kathmandu: Ekta books. vi+127 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Lamjung Yolmo is a tone language. It has only two tones, high and low, which are on the initial syllable of a word. There are some phonological constraints on tone, for example aspirated sounds are always high tone and voice sounds are always low tone. To distinguish the tones in the Latin script diacritics are use - so fa means hair and fd means pheasant. In the Devanagari diacritics are less practical, and so a % (h) appears after the initial vowel if the word is low tone and high tone is left unmarked. This is the preference of speakers.
tone_statements.locator: p. v, 'About Lamjung Yolmo' > 'Orthography' (tone paragraphs after the vowel table)
tone_statements.summary: Two tones, high and low, located on the word-initial syllable; aspirated onsets always high, voiced onsets always low. Low tone written with Devanagari h after the vowel; high unmarked.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated place in the Gawne 2016 PDF we hold (printed p.39, p.50; tone sec.3 p.33). (2) Deciding source: a 2016 sketch grammar (171 pp) by the language's principal documenter with a dedicated 'Stress' section; the identical statement is in her 2013 PhD grammar appendix (p.437, downloaded now), which is the Glottolog 'grammar' entry. No later or more specialised stress description exists in the Glottolog list; the one instrumental prosody study (Teo, Gawne & Baese-Berk 2015, downloaded) analyses only word-initial lexical tone plus phrasal intonation and never invokes stress, consistent with the no-word-stress coding and with the record's the primary-stress rule (binary H/L word tone on the first syllable). Gawne 2019 (downloaded) is silent on stress and repeats the word-initial tone statement. One nuance worth noting but not coding-changing: the 2013 thesis

tone.says: Verified from the PDF (sec. 'Tone', p. 6 of 23; 'Encyclopedic Review Article'): "Like other Tibetic languages, Yolmo has tone, which is located on the first vowel of a word. Hari presents a four tone contrast of Melamchi Valley Yolmo; high level, high falling, low level and low falling. Acoustic evidence from Lamjung Yolmo and Kagate indicates that there is only acoustic evidence for a contrast between two tones; low and high." Minimal pairs pu 'body hair' (H) / pu 'son' (L), komba 'thirsty' /…
